findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses AND instead of OR, excluding legitimate team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning a user must be BOTH a team admin AND the team owner simultaneously to pass this check. In practice a user is either an admin or the owner, so this condition is almost always false for team members who are 'only' an admin, contradicting the variable's name and intended semantics ('admin OR owner'). As a result, team admins who are not also the literal owner will be denied permission to add guests unless they happen to also be the booking organizer or an attendee, breaking the intended authorization model for team bookings.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw/unfiltered guest list instead of the deduplicated uniqueGuests
findings.body: After filtering out guests that are already attendees or blacklisted into `uniqueGuests` (used to actually create new attendees), the original unfiltered `guests` array is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` instead of `uniqueGuests`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), attendees are classified as 'new' vs 'existing' by checking membership in this list. If `guests` contains emails that were filtered out (already an attendee, blacklisted, or duplicate), those existing attendees will incorrectly be treated as newly added and sent the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` invite again instead of the intended `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification, producing confusing/duplicate invite emails.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing bypass via case variation
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but the incoming `guest` values from `guests` are compared as-is (`guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) without lower-casing `guest` first. A blacklisted address submitted with different letter casing (e.g. 'Admin@Example.com' vs 'admin@example.com') will not be filtered out, defeating the blacklist mechanism.

findings.title: Email send failure logged via console.log instead of the project logger
findings.body: On failure to send the add-guests emails, the error is only logged with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, swallowing the actual error object and not using the standard `@calcom/lib/logger` used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. in email-manager.ts). This makes failures hard to diagnose in production and is inconsistent with the rest of the handler's error-handling conventions.

findings.title: Error toast fallback message is unreachable dead code
findings.body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back to the friendlier localized message; it always shows the raw error code and message key concatenation to the end user, which can be confusing/unlocalized if `err.message` isn't a translation key that resolves properly.

findings.title: Dialog state (emails, invalid flag) is not reset when closed via outside click or Escape
findings.body: The `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail` state are only reset inside the explicit Cancel button's onClick handler. When the dialog is dismissed via the Dialog's `onOpenChange` (e.g. clicking outside or pressing Escape), `setIsOpenDialog` is called directly without clearing `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail`, so reopening the dialog later will show the previously entered (possibly invalid) email values and error state.

findings.title: No transaction/locking between read and write when adding attendees, risking duplicate attendee creation under concurrent requests
findings.body: The handler reads the booking's current attendees, computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, and then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` to insert them. If two add-guest requests for the same booking run concurrently (e.g. two different users clicking 'Add' at the same time with overlapping emails), both could compute the same 'unique' guest as not-yet-present and both insert it, resulting in duplicate attendee rows for the same email on the same booking, since there is no visible transaction or unique constraint enforcing (bookingId, email) uniqueness in this flow.

findings.title: No automated tests added for the new addGuests flow
findings.body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation (`addGuestsHandler`), a new client dialog (`AddGuestsDialog`), and a new reusable `MultiEmail` form component, but ships no unit or integration tests covering permission checks (organizer/attendee/team admin), duplicate/blacklist filtering, calendar update behavior, or the email dispatch logic (`sendAddGuestsEmails`). Given the authorization bug identified above, test coverage would likely have caught the issue before merge.
